# **High-Level Architecture and Cloud Topology**

**CampusNotes: Open-Access Academic Portal and AI-Powered Study Assistant**

Week 3 deliverable. It builds on the Week 2 Software Requirements Specification (SRS).

## **Table of Contents**

1. Introduction
2. System Boundary
3. Three-Tier Architecture
4. Data Flow Diagrams (Level 0 and Level 1)
5. Cloud Topology and Infrastructure Stack
6. Requirements-to-Architecture Traceability
7. Conclusion

---

# **1. Introduction**

This document describes the high-level architecture of CampusNotes. It shows how the system is divided into a client, an API server and a database (three tiers), how data moves through the system (Data Flow Diagrams), where the system boundary lies, and which cloud services will host it and why they were chosen.

All decisions here are made to satisfy the functional requirements (FR-01 to FR-12) and the quantified non-functional requirements (NFR-01 to NFR-13) of the Week 2 SRS.

**Design assumption.** CampusNotes has no student accounts (FR-04, NFR-06). Therefore the student's reading progress and quiz results are kept in the browser's local storage on the student's own device. Courses, modules, MCQs, cached AI summaries and admin accounts are stored in the cloud database. If server-side progress analytics are needed later, a progress table keyed by an anonymous session ID can be added without changing the three tiers.

# **2. System Boundary**

The system boundary separates what the project team builds and controls (inside) from the people and services it only talks to (outside). The red dashed line in Figure 1 and the single system process in the Level 0 part of the DFD (Figure 2) show this boundary.

## **2.1 Inside and Outside the Boundary**

| Inside the boundary (built and controlled by the team)                 | Outside the boundary (external)                                      |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Web client: the Next.js / React user interface sent to the browser     | Student (human user)                                                 |
| Admin Panel (`/admin`)                                                 | System Administrator (human user)                                    |
| API server: Next.js server routes running on Node.js                   | AI Summarization Service (third-party API)                           |
| Database: courses, modules, MCQ bank, AI summaries, admin accounts     | The user's device and browser runtime                                |
| Course content and MCQ banks loaded by the administrator               | Cloud provider platform services (hosting, CDN, managed database)    |

## **2.2 Interfaces that Cross the Boundary**

| ID | From to To                          | Protocol and data                                                                                         |
|----|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| I1 | Student to System, and back         | HTTPS (TLS 1.3). Search / filter queries, module selections, summary requests, quiz answers. Returns course lists, notes, summaries, quiz feedback and score reports. |
| I2 | Administrator to System, and back   | HTTPS (TLS 1.3). Login credentials and course / module / MCQ data. Returns login result and management status. |
| I3 | System to AI Service, and back      | HTTPS POST from the server only. Sends module text. Receives a summary and 4 key takeaways. The API key stays in the server environment and never reaches the browser. |

---

# **3. Three-Tier Architecture**

CampusNotes uses a three-tier architecture. Each tier has one job and talks only to the tier next to it. The browser never connects to the database directly.

![Figure 1: Three-Tier Architecture Diagram][img1]

*Figure 1: Three-Tier Architecture Diagram of CampusNotes.*

## **3.1 Tier Responsibilities**

| Tier                 | Responsibility                                                                                                             | Technology                                       |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Tier 1: Client       | Shows the course catalog, module reader, AI summary drawer, quiz screens and admin panel. Gives instant green / red quiz feedback. Keeps progress and quiz attempts in local storage. | Next.js (App Router), React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS |
| Tier 2: API Server   | Serves pages and JSON APIs. Validates and sanitizes all input. Calls the AI service. Scores quizzes. Authenticates the administrator. | Next.js server routes on Node.js                 |
| Tier 3: Database     | Stores courses, modules, MCQ bank, cached AI summaries and admin accounts. Keeps quiz questions separated by subject.        | Managed relational database (PostgreSQL)         |

## **3.2 Why Three Tiers**

- **Separation of concerns.** The interface, the logic and the data can change independently.
- **Security.** Only the API server can reach the database and the AI key, so the browser cannot expose them (supports NFR-05, NFR-07, NFR-08).
- **Scalability.** The API server can scale out for exam-time traffic without touching the database design (supports NFR-04).
- **Fault isolation.** If the AI service fails, tiers 1 to 3 still serve notes and quizzes (supports NFR-11).

Notation: green boxes are external actors, circles are processes, cylinders are data stores in the cloud database, purple rounded boxes are data stores in the student's browser, the orange box is an external service, and the dashed line is the system boundary. Blue arrows carry data into the system, green arrows carry data out of the system, and grey arrows are flows inside the system. Every flow has a number so it can be found in the tables below.

*Figure 2: Data Flow Diagram (Level 0 and Level 1) of CampusNotes.*

## **4.1 DFD Level 0 (Context Diagram)**

The whole system is one process. Only the data entering and leaving it is drawn. The database is drawn beside the system for clarity, but it belongs inside the system boundary (Section 2).

| Flow | From           | To             | Data                                                                                   |
|------|----------------|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1    | Student        | System         | Search / filter query, module selection, summary request, quiz answers                 |
| 2    | System         | Student        | Course list, module notes, AI summary, quiz feedback and explanations, score report    |
| 3    | Administrator  | System         | Login credentials, course / module / MCQ data                                          |
| 4    | System         | Administrator  | Login result, management status                                                        |
| 5    | System         | Database       | Read / write data (courses, modules, MCQs, summaries, admin accounts)                  |
| 6    | Database       | System         | Data results                                                                           |
| 7    | System         | AI Service     | Module text (HTTPS)                                                                    |
| 8    | AI Service     | System         | Summary and 4 key takeaways                                                            |

## **4.2 DFD Level 1**

Level 1 splits the single process of Level 0 into five processes and shows the six data stores they use.

### **Processes**

| ID  | Process                      | What it does                                                                                              | Reads / writes        | Use case (SRS)        |
|-----|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
| 1.0 | Browse and Search Courses    | Returns the course catalog and applies the student's search text and category filter                      | Reads D1              | UC-01, UC-02, UC-03, UC-04 |
| 2.0 | Read Modules and Track Progress | Returns module notes, records completed modules and the last visited module                            | Reads D1; reads and writes D5 | UC-05, UC-06  |
| 3.0 | Generate AI Summary          | Takes the active module text, asks the AI service for a summary and 4 takeaways, caches the result, shows a fallback notice if the service takes 2.5 s or more | Reads and writes D3   | UC-07                 |
| 4.0 | Conduct Quiz                 | Loads the MCQs of one subject, validates each answer instantly, returns the explanation and the final score | Reads D2; writes D6   | UC-08, UC-09          |
| 5.0 | Manage Content (Admin)       | Checks admin credentials, then adds, edits and removes courses, modules and MCQs                          | Reads D4; writes D1, D2 | UC-10, UC-11, UC-12 |

### **Data Stores**

| ID | Data store         | Contents                                                           | Location                              |
|----|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| D1 | Courses and Modules | Course code, title, category; module title, order and content (drawn twice in Figure 2 so that no line crosses the diagram) | Cloud database                        |
| D2 | MCQ Bank           | Questions, 4 options, correct option, explanation, subject         | Cloud database                        |
| D3 | AI Summaries       | Summary text, 4 key takeaways, saved date, linked module           | Cloud database                        |
| D4 | Admin Accounts     | Admin identity and salted password hash                            | Cloud database                        |
| D5 | Progress           | Completed modules, last visited module                             | Browser local storage (student device) |
| D6 | Quiz Results       | Score, correct and incorrect counts, attempt date                  | Browser local storage (student device) |

### **Level 1 Data Flows**

| Flow | From     | To       | Data                                              |
|------|----------|----------|---------------------------------------------------|
| 1    | Student  | 1.0      | Search / filter query                             |
| 2    | 1.0      | Student  | Course list and details                           |
| 3    | Student  | 2.0      | Module selection                                  |
| 4    | 2.0      | Student  | Module notes and progress                         |
| 5    | Student  | 3.0      | Summary request                                   |
| 6    | 3.0      | Student  | Summary and 4 key takeaways                       |
| 7    | Student  | 4.0      | Quiz answers                                      |
| 8    | 4.0      | Student  | Feedback, explanation, score report               |
| 9    | D1       | 1.0      | Course data                                       |
| 10   | D1       | 2.0      | Module content                                    |
| 11   | 2.0      | 3.0      | Active module text                                |
| 12   | 2.0      | D5       | Save progress (and read saved progress back)      |
| 13   | 3.0      | AI Service | Module text (HTTPS)                             |
| 14   | AI Service | 3.0    | Summary and 4 key takeaways                       |
| 15   | 3.0      | D3       | Save summary (and read cached summary back)       |
| 16   | D2       | 4.0      | MCQs, answers, explanations                       |
| 17   | 4.0      | D6       | Quiz result                                       |
| 18   | Administrator | 5.0 | Login credentials, course / module / MCQ data    |
| 19   | 5.0      | Administrator | Login result, management status             |
| 20   | D4       | 5.0      | Credential check                                  |
| 21   | 5.0      | D2       | MCQ data                                          |
| 22   | 5.0      | D1       | Course / module data                              |

### **Balancing Check (Level 0 and Level 1)**

The flows between the system and the outside world are the same at both levels. Level 0 flows 1 and 2 (Student) are split into Level 1 flows 1 to 8 through processes 1.0 to 4.0. Level 0 flows 3 and 4 (Administrator) become Level 1 flows 18 and 19 through process 5.0. Level 0 flows 7 and 8 (AI Service) become Level 1 flows 13 and 14 through process 3.0. Level 0 flows 5 and 6 (database) are the reads and writes of the processes to D1 to D4 (Level 1 flows 9, 10, 15, 16, 20, 21 and 22). No external entity or flow was added or dropped when the diagram was decomposed.

# **5. Cloud Topology and Infrastructure Stack**

The topology in Figure 3 shows where each part of CampusNotes runs and how traffic reaches it.

![Figure 3: Cloud Topology Diagram][img3]

*Figure 3: Cloud Topology of CampusNotes.*

**How a request travels.** The student's browser reaches the site over HTTPS. DNS and the CDN edge answer for static files (JavaScript, CSS, images) and end the TLS 1.3 connection. Page and API requests that are not cached go to the serverless application platform, where Next.js renders pages and runs the API routes as Node.js functions. The API routes query the managed PostgreSQL database over an encrypted connection and, for summaries, call the external AI service from the server. Source code is stored in a Git repository and a CI/CD pipeline builds, tests and deploys every change. An uptime monitor watches the live site.

## **5.1 Infrastructure Stack and Justification**

| Layer                   | Choice                                                             | Justification                                                                                                              | Supports      |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
| Frontend framework      | Next.js (App Router), React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS           | One codebase for pages and APIs. Pages can be pre-rendered so first paint does not wait for a server. Tailwind gives responsive layouts from 320 px to 2560 px. | NFR-01, NFR-12 |
| Hosting                 | Serverless application platform built for Next.js (for example Vercel) | No servers to manage. Deploys straight from Git. Scales automatically when many students revise before exams. Managed HTTPS certificates. | NFR-04, NFR-05, NFR-09 |
| CDN and edge            | Provider's built-in CDN and edge network                           | Serves static files close to the user, which lowers load time on mobile networks and campus Wi-Fi.                          | NFR-01        |
| Database                | Managed PostgreSQL (for example Neon or Supabase)                  | The data model is relational (courses, modules, quizzes, MCQs with foreign keys). PostgreSQL gives strong integrity and JSON columns for MCQ options and takeaways. A managed service gives backups and patching without extra effort. | NFR-09, NFR-10 |
| AI summarization        | Third-party language-model API, called only from the server        | Produces good summaries without training a model. The server holds the key and applies a 2.5 s timeout, so a slow response never blocks reading or quizzes. | NFR-03, NFR-11 |
| Secrets management      | Platform environment variables                                     | Keeps the AI key and database URL out of the source code and out of the browser.                                            | NFR-07, NFR-08 |
| Source control and CI/CD | GitHub with automatic build and deploy                            | Every change is tested and deployed the same way. Preview deployments let the supervisor see work before release.          | Maintainability |
| Monitoring              | Uptime monitor with alerts, plus platform logs                     | Measures the 99.5% availability target and the latency targets with real data.                                             | NFR-09, NFR-01, NFR-03 |

Before the final choice, the team shall confirm each provider's current free-tier limits and published availability, because these can change.

## **5.2 Alternatives Considered**

| Decision  | Alternative                | Why it was not chosen                                                                                          |
|-----------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Hosting   | Virtual machine (VPS) that the team administers | Needs manual setup of TLS, patching, scaling and monitoring, which is too much operations work for a student project. |
| Hosting   | Full cloud suite with separate load balancer, servers and CDN | More powerful but much more to configure and more to go wrong for the expected load.           |
| Database  | Document database (NoSQL) | The data is strongly relational and quizzes must never mix subjects, which foreign keys enforce easily.        |
| Database  | File-based database (SQLite) | Does not suit serverless functions that run on many short-lived instances.                                  |

## **5.3 Risks and Mitigations**

| Risk                                                      | Mitigation                                                                                           |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cold starts of serverless functions slow the first page   | Pre-render course and module pages and serve them from the CDN so FCP stays at 1.2 s or less         |
| Many short-lived functions exhaust database connections   | Use connection pooling or a serverless database driver                                               |
| AI service is slow, down or costly                        | 2.5 s timeout with a fallback notice, plus caching of summaries in D3 so each module is summarized once |
| Free-tier limits reached during exams                     | Watch usage in monitoring and be ready to move to a paid tier                                        |
| Vendor lock-in                                            | Use standard Next.js and standard PostgreSQL so the system can move to another host                  |

# **6. Requirements-to-Architecture Traceability**

| Requirement (from SRS)                                  | Architecture decision that satisfies it                                                          |
|---------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NFR-01: FCP of 1.2 s or less                            | Pre-rendered pages, CDN edge caching                                                             |
| NFR-02: UI interaction within 150 ms                    | Filtering and quiz validation run in the browser (Tier 1)                                        |
| NFR-03: AI summary within 2.5 s                         | Server-side AI call with 2.5 s timeout, cached summaries (D3)                                    |
| NFR-04: 200 simultaneous students                       | Serverless auto-scaling, pooled database connections                                             |
| NFR-05: 100% HTTPS with TLS 1.3                         | TLS terminated at the edge with managed certificates                                             |
| NFR-06: zero PII from students                          | No student accounts; progress and results stay in local storage (D5, D6)                         |
| NFR-07: sanitized input, 0 XSS / injection findings     | Validation and sanitization layer in the API server                                              |
| NFR-08: hashed admin passwords, 30-minute session       | Admin API and Auth with salted hashes (D4) and session timeout                                   |
| NFR-09: 99.5% availability                              | Managed hosting and database, automated backups, uptime monitoring                               |
| NFR-10: 0% cross-subject quiz questions                 | MCQ bank (D2) queried by subject and quiz ID only                                                |
| NFR-11: graceful degradation when AI fails              | AI call isolated in process 3.0 with timeout and fallback notice                                 |
| NFR-12, NFR-13: responsive and accessible UI            | Tailwind CSS responsive layout and contrast-checked design in Tier 1                             |

---

# **7. Conclusion**

CampusNotes is organized as a client, an API server and a database. The Level 0 DFD shows its boundary with three external parties: students, the administrator and the AI service. The Level 1 DFD breaks the system into five processes and six data stores, and balances with Level 0. The proposed cloud stack, a Next.js serverless platform with a CDN, managed PostgreSQL, a server-side AI call, CI/CD and uptime monitoring, was chosen because it meets the performance, security and availability targets of the SRS with very little server administration. The editable draw.io source of each diagram is supplied as a separate file.
